title: Homogeneous degree-zero localization commutes with scalar extension
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with a ring homomorphism $R\to S$. Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring with a ring map $R\to A_0$. Put $C=S\otimes_R A$, with multiplication $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes b)=st\otimes ab$ and grading $C_n=S\otimes_R A_n$. For any homogeneous $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, put $f_S=1\otimes f$. Degree-zero homogeneous localization has the fraction notation of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. The formula $$\lambda_f:S\otimes_R A_{(f),0}\longrightarrow C_{(f_S),0},\qquad s\otimes(a/f^m)\longmapsto (s\otimes a)/f_S^m\quad(a\in A_{md})$$ defines an isomorphism of $S$-algebras. No flatness assumption on $S$ over $R$ and no regularity assumption on $f$ is required.

proof.text: The graded ring map a ↦ 1 ⊗ a induces a ring map on homogeneous localizations, compatible with the R-algebra structures by compatibility with the degree-zero maps. The tensor algebra universal property gives an S-algebra map λ. The homogeneous fraction map formula and scalar multiplication give λ(s ⊗ (a/f^m)) = (s ⊗ a)/(1 ⊗ f)^m.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), standard-open calculation; fraction convention of Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open)

proof.text: For m ≥ 0 let u_m:A_(md) → H be the R-linear map a ↦ a/f^m, and put q_m = S ⊗ u_m. Multiplication by f^k defines an R-linear transition T_(m,k):A_(md) → A_((m+k)d). The ordinary fraction relation gives u_(m+k) T_(m,k) = u_m. Tensor induction gives q_(m+k)(S ⊗ T_(m,k))(c) = q_m(c). Tensor induction also shows that every x in S ⊗ H is q_m(c) for some m,c: pure tensors use a fraction presentation of their second factor, and sums pass from denominators m,n to m+n using these transitions.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), standard-open calculation; fraction convention of Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open)

proof.text: The canonical map β_m:S ⊗ A_(md) → C_(md) is bijective: the decomposition of A as a direct sum of its graded pieces remains a direct sum after tensoring, so each graded inclusion remains split. This is Mathlib DirectSum.toBaseChange_bijective. Tensor induction proves λ(q_m(c)) = β_m(c)/(1 ⊗ f)^m, and β_(m+k)((S ⊗ T_(m,k))(c)) = β_m(c)(1 ⊗ f)^k. Every target fraction has numerator in a base-changed graded piece, hence is λ(q_m(c)) for a preimage c under β_m. Thus λ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), standard-open calculation; fraction convention of Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open)

proof.text: If λ(x)=0, write x=q_m(c). The ordinary localization zero criterion gives k such that (1 ⊗ f)^k β_m(c)=0. By the transition formula and injectivity of β_(m+k), (S ⊗ T_(m,k))(c)=0. Applying q_(m+k) and its transition identity yields x=0. Since λ is additive, trivial kernel gives injectivity. Promote the bijective S-algebra homomorphism to an S-algebra equivalence; its fraction formula is the one proved in step 1. No cancellation, flatness, or nonzero denominator hypothesis is used.
